LESSON: IMITATIVE SPEAKING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Listening and speaking
Topic 1.2: Imitative speaking
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Imitative speaking, part of Listening and speaking in Grade 5 GERMAN.

Key inquiry question: Why is imitation in a language important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to/watch a simple audio/video on a nuclear family (Vater, Mutter, Eltern, Kind, Sohn, Tochter, Bruder, Schwester, Geschwister) introducing each other,

2. ask and respond to questions on names of nuclear family members with peers (z.B Wie heißt dein/e....? mein/e ......heisst.,

3. listen to peers reading out aloud short sentences on nuclear family(z.B Das ist der Vater/die Mutter. Er /sie heisst...,

4. listen to and repeat dialogues on nuclear family members' names.

5. recite/sing short poems/songs on family

6. describe members of the nuclear family to peers (z.B Der Vater ist nett...)

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to/watch a simple audio/video on a nuclear family (Vater, Mutter, Eltern, Kind, Sohn, Tochter, Bruder, Schwester, Geschwister) introducing each other,
2. ask and respond to questions on names of nuclear family members with peers (z.B Wie heißt dein/e....? mein/e ......heisst.,
3. listen to peers reading out aloud short sentences on nuclear family(z.B Das ist der Vater/die Mutter. Er /sie heisst...,
4. listen to and repeat dialogues on nuclear family members' names.
5. recite/sing short poems/songs on family
6. describe members of the nuclear family to peers (z.B Der Vater ist nett...)

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Imitative speaking together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Self-efficacy: The learner develops assertiveness as they describe members of the nuclear family to peers.

Values:
Love: The learner demonstrates love for their family as they describe members of the nuclear family to peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Citizenship: The learner appreciates diversity in the nuclear family as they talk about own family with peers.

Link to other Learning Areas

The learner links the concept of nuclear family to the same concept in Social Studies and Religious Education.
